items.description: The `ArgoCDTools` repo exists with the presync entrypoint, its support code and the Dockerfile — and it is a working repo of this estate: its own `.kubecoder/project.yaml` with `jenkins: IaC/ArgoCDTools`, whose lint and test verbs are green from the repo root.
items.rationale: `.kubecoder/project.yaml` exists with `jenkins: IaC/ArgoCDTools` (line 11), lint verbs `cexec iac ruff check .` + `cexec iac ruff format --check .` (12-14) and test verb `cexec iac python3 -m unittest discover -b -s tests -t .` (18), read directly. Lint and test are established GREEN via sweep r2 (ArgoCDTools_root_lint.log, ArgoCDTools_root_test.log) on the pushed commit.

items.area: R1 — the flow: clone at SHA
items.description: The entrypoint clones the deploy repo at exactly the SHA it was handed, and that is the run's only clone. The clone authenticates via an inline credential helper, never a token-in-URL remote.
items.rationale: `presync/git.py` clones via `init` (21) + `remote add origin <url>` (24, no embedded credential) + `fetch --depth 1 origin <revision>` (25-41) + `checkout --detach FETCH_HEAD` (42), then checks `rev-parse HEAD` against the argument and raises on mismatch (44-46). The credential helper is passed per-command via `git -c`, with an empty `-c credential.helper=` immediately ahead of the real one (30-33) so no ambient helper in the run's `HOME` is consulted — `tests/test_git.py:55-78` proves this against a `HOME` carrying its own helper. Confirmed by direct code read; suite green in sweep r2.

items.area: R1 — the flow: the state backend
items.description: The entrypoint starts terraform-backend-git on localhost inside its own process space, waits for it to accept, and points Terraform at it through `-backend-config` address/lock_address/unlock_address at init — pointed at the same state repo and keying as `iac`. The state key is `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/terraform.tfstate`.
items.rationale: `presync/backend.py`: daemon spawned on `127.0.0.1:6061` (26,90) with a bounded 10s wait (`_wait_until_listening`, 32,95-108); `PRESYNC_TF_BACKEND` (30) reuses an already-listening backend instead of spawning one (75-92). State key is `f"argocd/{repo_name(repo_url)}/{stage}/terraform.tfstate"` (52-54), `<repo>` = last URL path segment minus `.git` (44-49). State repo/ref are constants `https://github.com/pvginkel/TerraformState` @ `main` (22-23). Confirmed by direct code read; suite green in sweep r2.

items.area: R1 — the flow: terraform init/apply with the stage tfvars
items.description: `terraform init && terraform apply` runs in the clone's `terraform/`, and every `config/<stage>/*.tfvars` in the clone reaches that apply — the tfvars come off the hook's own disk and never travel through Argo (D14).
items.rationale: `presync/terraform.py`: `init`/`apply` both run with `-chdir=<clone>/terraform` (21-26,60-78). Every `config/<stage>/*.tfvars` in the clone is collected sorted (`var_files`, 29-38) and passed as absolute `-var-file=` paths (66-78, comment at 67 states why absolute is required under `-chdir`). Tfvars never travel through Argo (D14) — they come off the clone's own disk. Confirmed by direct code read plus `tests/test_terraform.py:39-46` and `tests/test_cli.py:115-123`; suite green in sweep r2.

items.description: The entrypoint synthesises a kubeconfig from the pod's own ServiceAccount and exports both `KUBE_CONFIG_PATH` and `KUBECONFIG` at it before `terraform init`, so a bare `provider "kubernetes" {}` configures itself from that file. The proof asserts the synthesis and its selection over any ambient kubeconfig — a result that would also hold via this pod's `~/.kube/config` proves nothing.
items.rationale: `presync/kubeconfig.py`: `identity()` (48-59) reads the projected SA `token`/`ca.crt` plus `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`/`_PORT`, raising `PresyncError` on a missing SA with no fallback to any ambient kubeconfig. `provide()` (62-69) writes the file and sets **both** `KUBE_CONFIG_PATH` and `KUBECONFIG` in `os.environ` (37,66-67) before `init` (cli.py:35 precedes cli.py:44). `PRESYNC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_DIR` (29,50) overrides the source directory for out-of-cluster runs. The selection-over-ambient claim is not just inferred: `tests/test_kubeconfig.py:49-55` and `tests/test_cli.py:125-134` assert the minted values win even when an ambient `KUBECONFIG`/`~/.kube/config` is pre-set. P2's done-record additionally documents a live run from this pod against the real apiserver, TLS-verified against the SA CA, refused on the placeholder token.

items.description: The reattach finds `Released` PVs whose `claimRef` names the run's target namespace and nulls `claimRef.uid`/`resourceVersion`, leaving PVs outside that namespace untouched. The namespace is the fourth Job argument, used as given — the hook derives it from nothing. Exercised against a deliberately-`Released` PV on the prd cluster (the operator's 2026-08-14 amendment), inside the throwaway `presync-proof` fixture the ruling scopes — two namespaces and hostPath PVs the proof creates and deletes, with no PV outside the fixture touched. The fixture's cluster-scoped objects are created over SSH (`sudo microk8s kubectl` on `srvk8s1`, per `docs/live-infra-access.md`), because the mounted `~/.kube/config-prd-write` is namespaced-edit only and can create neither a PV nor a namespace.
items.rationale: `presync/reattach.py.claimed_by()` (28-39) matches `status.phase == Released` **and** `spec.claimRef.namespace` **equal to** (not prefix of) the given namespace, nulling `claimRef.uid`/`resourceVersion` via a JSON merge-patch (25,48) sent by `presync/kube.py`'s `Api` over stdlib `urllib`/`ssl` only — no kubectl, no k8s client library. `cli.py:44-50` applies before reattaching, explicitly ordered. `Api.__init__` (kube.py:29-38) clears only `ssl.VERIFY_X509_STRICT` (the estate CA has no `keyUsage` extension) — chain, expiry and hostname verification stay on. `tests/test_reattach.py:33-39` proves a prefix-sibling namespace is not matched; `:90-99` proves the token is re-read per request; `:115-122` proves an untrusted CA is still refused. This code path is unchanged since P3, whose done-record documents the actual live proof on the prd cluster (throwaway `presync-proof` fixture: exactly the one matching Released/target-namespace PV reattached, the sibling and same-namespace-Bound PV untouched, all 47 pre-existing PVs including 8 real Released ones unchanged by resourceVersion). That live prd fixture (creating/deleting cluster-scoped objects over SSH) was not re-run this test pass — it mutates prd and the dispatch keeps prd operator-gated; the unit-level proof plus the unmodified live-proof record are treated as the standing evidence, per this repo's testing doctrine that real-infra proof is the operator's/already-run province, not something to re-trigger without cause.

items.description: The entrypoint exits non-zero when any step of the flow fails and zero only when the apply succeeded — proven on both paths, including a deliberate failure, so a swallowed failure could not pass.
items.rationale: `presync/__main__.py` turns a `PresyncError` into `sys.exit(1)`; `main()` returns 0 on success. `tests/test_cli.py`'s `ExitCodeTests` (195-222) runs the real `python3 -m presync` subprocess and asserts `returncode == 0` on a clean apply (207) and `returncode == 1` with the run's actual last stderr line naming the failure (212-222) — not merely a progress line, per P9's mutation-confirmed fix. Confirmed by direct code read; suite green in sweep r2.

items.description: A real entrypoint run from this pod exercises clone-at-SHA → backend → `init`/`apply` → exit code against a throwaway deploy repo and a scratch state key, on both the success and the deliberate-failure path. No Argo CD, no `argocd-hooks` namespace and no OpenBao credentials are needed for it — the run sets the environment variables directly.
items.rationale: The suite is a live proof, not a full mock: `ExitCodeTests` (tests/test_cli.py) runs the real `python3 -m presync` end to end against a throwaway git-served deploy repo, and `ReleaseIdentityTests` (tests/test_terraform.py:117-167) runs the real Terraform 1.15.8 binary. Both the success path (exit 0) and the deliberate-failure path (exit 1, named cause) are exercised, with no Argo CD, no `argocd-hooks` namespace and no OpenBao credentials — environment variables are set directly by the tests/fixtures. `kc project test` for ArgoCDTools/root is established GREEN in sweep r2, and P1/P2's done-records additionally record the same flow proven interactively from this pod during development.

items.description: The Dockerfile bakes exactly what the job needs to run and nothing general-purpose — the four D31 names plus the distro `python3` the entrypoint runs under, `librados2`/`librbd1` for the cgo `pvginkel/homelab` binary, the Terraform CLI config routing that provider to the estate's mirror, and the step-ca root the mirror's chain needs — and nothing is cloned at runtime except the deploy repo. Terraform is unpinned from the hashicorp `noble` suite and terraform-backend-git is pinned to v0.1.11, as `iac` does both. `support/iac-image/` and the `iac` image are untouched.
items.rationale: `Dockerfile` (read in full): `ubuntu:noble` base; Terraform installed unpinned from the hashicorp noble suite (43-46); `terraform-backend-git` v0.1.11 via `COPY --from` (55-56); git, distro python3, librados2, librbd1 via apt (30-38); `image/terraform.rc` at `/etc/terraform.rc` with `TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE` (16,70); `image/homelab-root.crt` installed into the trust store (58-64); `USER ubuntu` (77) with a build-time `RUN` asserting `getent passwd "$(id -u)"`, terraform, terraform-backend-git, git, `import presync.cli` and a `CDLL` load of both `librados.so.2`/`librbd.so.1` (84-89); `ENTRYPOINT ["python3","-m","presync"]` (91). `Jenkinsfile`: `podTemplate(inheritFrom: 'jenkins-agent kaniko')` → `container('kaniko')` → `helmCharts.kaniko2(destinations: ["registry:5000/argocd-hook:${currentBuild.number}", "registry:5000/argocd-hook:latest"])` (13-29), `disableConcurrentBuilds()`+`githubPush()` (9-10), exactly two stages, no deploy stage. `.dockerignore` excludes `*.md`, `tests`, `ruff.toml`, `.kubecoder`. `git diff eacb2d0..cd4fded --stat -- support/iac-image/` is empty — the `iac` image is untouched. Matches D31 as amended by P11.

items.description: CI publishes `registry:5000/argocd-hook:<n>` — a push to `ArgoCDTools` triggers `IaC/ArgoCDTools`, the build succeeds, and the numbered tag is in the registry.
items.rationale: `ArgoCDTools` was pushed to `origin/main` this session (new branch, commit `98ce20f`). No `IaC/ArgoCDTools` Jenkins job exists — confirmed via `getJob` and `findJobsWithScmUrl` against `git@github.com:pvginkel/ArgoCDTools.git`, both empty, checked both before and after the push. This is the exact gap the plan's own ordering constraint anticipated ("the run does not pause for it") and matches a pre-existing tracked card. No image tag can be observed in the registry until the job exists and builds. Owed: the operator hand-creates `IaC/ArgoCDTools` (folder `IaC`, SCM `https://github.com/pvginkel/ArgoCDTools.git`, Script Path `Jenkinsfile`, `githubPush()` trigger already in the Jenkinsfile) mirroring the `IaC/Charts` precedent, then triggers a first build — either "Build Now" or a trivial follow-up push, since the push that should have triggered it already happened before the job existed.

items.area: R2 — the default pin lands in the library chart
items.description: The library chart's values carry the default hook image pin and it names the actual first `IaC/ArgoCDTools` build — the two repos' first releases coordinated, per the inherited ruling that 007 owns confirming or correcting the number.
items.rationale: `charts/homelab-shared/values.yaml:7` carries `imageTag: "1"`, consumed by `_tf-presync-hook.tpl:43` (`$hook.imageTag | default $lib.imageTag`) — present and internally consistent, confirmed by direct read. Whether "1" actually names `IaC/ArgoCDTools`'s real first build cannot be confirmed until that job exists and runs (see V10) — owed to the operator. Per the ruling, the pin is not correctable after the fact if wrong (the 0.2.0 tarball is already committed and immutable); a wrong guess costs a 0.3.0 republish, which is the ruling's named accepted cost, not this test phase's to pay.

items.description: The entrypoint's argument contract and the library chart's Job template agree on four arguments — repo, revision, stage, namespace — each `required`-guarded in the template, so a chart that forgets one fails to render rather than passing an empty argument, and in that order, since the entrypoint takes them positionally. The guard and the order assertion are shown to bite, not assumed to.
items.rationale: `presync/cli.py:22-25` adds arguments in order repo, revision, stage, namespace (`tests/test_cli.py:36-43`). `charts/homelab-shared/templates/_tf-presync-hook.tpl:45-48` renders four `required`-guarded args in the same order. `tests/render-consumer.sh:73-89` asserts the rendered `args:` block as a whole ordered, length-checked sequence via an indentation-agnostic awk extraction — not four independent per-line greps — and P10's done-record mutation-confirms it catches both a swap and a dropped argument. Both halves of the contract agree, and the gate is proven (not merely trusted) to bite.

items.description: `homelab-shared` publishes as 0.2.0: the version bumped, the new tarball committed to `dist/`, the already-published 0.1.0 tarball unmodified in tree and history, and the repo's own publish and render gates green.
items.rationale: `charts/homelab-shared/Chart.yaml:7` reads `version: 0.2.0`. `dist/homelab-shared-0.2.0.tgz` exists (sha256 `8cdba732...`, matching its committed bytes). `dist/homelab-shared-0.1.0.tgz` is byte-identical between its original commit `6da54f8` and the current working tree (sha256 `5405a96d...` both), and `git log --all --diff-filter=MDR -- 'dist/*.tgz'` returns no modify/delete/rename ever, for either tarball — hash-verified independently of the gate. `tests/publish.sh:50-53` (missing-tarball) and `:111-123` (working-tree + history immutability) are read and confirmed to catch either violation.

items.description: The hook's credentials are its own, minted deliberately, and delivered as plain environment variables: the container knows nothing about OpenBao, AppRoles or any credential provider. **No AppRole is minted** — no hvac, no `!bao` resolver, no secrets manifest in the image. Configuration arrives the same way: `ArgoCDTools` commits no estate facts — no copy of `clusters.yaml`, no Ceph mon host, S3 endpoint, `zfs_pools` map or age recipient anywhere in the repo — and a value the run needs but did not get fails the run by name rather than reaching Terraform as an empty string.
items.rationale: Repo-wide greps across `/work/ArgoCDTools` for a Ceph mon host pattern, an S3 endpoint pattern, `zfs_pools`, an `age1…` recipient string, and any `clusters.yaml` copy all return empty, except a fake test-fixture IP (`10.152.183.1`, `tests/test_kubeconfig.py`) and the deliberately-included, non-cluster-fact `tfmirror.home` hostname in `image/terraform.rc` (reviewed and accepted in P4, not a `clusters.yaml` value). `presync/environment.py:5` states outright that the container knows nothing about OpenBao, AppRoles or any credential provider.

items.description: The inventory is complete against the estate's Terraform capabilities and settled to the key name: every key the container reads, the OpenBao leaf and property behind each secret, and — for the non-secret per-cluster facts the same ExternalSecret carries as `template` literals — the `clusters.yaml` value each one is copied from. It is what slice 009 authors the ExternalSecret from, so the names are unambiguous and nothing the run needs is missing from the one object that composes its environment.
items.rationale: Every environment variable `presync` reads via `environment.require()` — `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GIT_USERNAME` (cli.py:31-32), `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`/`_PORT` (kubeconfig.py:57-58, pod-injected, outside the inventory's scope by design), `TF_BACKEND_HTTP_ENCRYPTION_PROVIDER`/`TF_BACKEND_HTTP_SOPS_AGE_RECIPIENTS`/`SOPS_AGE_KEY` (backend.py:38-40,83-84) — maps to a named row in `attachments/credential-inventory.md`, or to a documented dev-only override (`PRESYNC_TF_BACKEND`, `PRESYNC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_DIR`, never set in the Job). Inventory rows the code does not itself read (`HOMELAB_*` provider credentials/config, `TF_VAR_postgres_admin_password`) are consumed directly by the `homelab`/`postgresql` Terraform providers via `envFrom`, exactly as the inventory and P2's done-record ("provider credentials pass through untouched") describe — not a gap.

items.description: The git token's required permissions are stated precisely enough for the operator to mint it: state repo read-write, deploy repos read-only, plus `admin:repo_hook` per D39/D41.
items.rationale: `attachments/credential-inventory.md` "The GitHub PAT" section states the three required permissions precisely: `pvginkel/TerraformState` read-write, every deploy repo read-only, every deploy repo `admin:repo_hook` — with the fine-grained-PAT rationale (a classic `repo` scope would over-grant). Cross-checked against `argo-cd/decisions.md` D39 (:334-343, the `admin:repo_hook`/webhook-as-Terraform-resource rationale) and D41 (:360-377, the state/deploy-repo read-write/read-only split) — both support the claim as stated. The mint itself is the operator's, outside this criterion's subject.

items.description: The state encryption key is `iac`'s existing age keypair, readable by the prd `eso` AppRole — one keypair in one leaf, so no rotation can leave state that one side of the same state repo cannot decrypt. The private half is fetched from that leaf and the public half is a `template` literal, so the leaf is written to by nobody and the operator's handover carries no conditional. The Ansible change granting the read is the only OpenBao policy change the slice makes; every other leaf in the inventory is already covered.
items.rationale:
Code verified: `ansible/inventories/prd/group_vars/openbao.yml` (commit `dee1c87`) appends exactly one leaf, `iac/tf-backend`, to `openbao_eso_kv_paths`, with a block comment stating why it is shared rather than copied. `roles/openbao/tasks/approle.yml:150-211` renders the `eso` policy from that list and only PUTs when the rendered text differs (194-211, idempotent by construction, no new command/shell task added) — the write task carries no `check_mode: false`, so `--check` would report the change without applying it (honest check-mode). `templates/policy.hcl.j2` grants `read` on `kv/data/

` and `read`+`list` on `kv/metadata/

` per entry, nothing special needed for a single non-glob leaf. `ansible`/`architecture` gates are established GREEN in sweep r2, and `iac-on-push` (`IaC/Build-Main` build #133, verified via `getBuildChangeSets` to be triggered by this exact commit) is SUCCESS. Not verified live: the grant only exists in OpenBao once the operator runs `cd /work/Ansible/ansible && cexec iac poetry run ansible-playbook playbooks/site-openbao.yml` against prd — explicitly operator-gated (prd) per the dispatch, and no `ansible-playbook`/`bao` command was run against live OpenBao this session.

items.description: The operator writes the secret values: the slice hands over the exact `bao` commands, the paths and the PAT permissions, and no agent runs `ansible-playbook`, writes an OpenBao value, or mints a token.
items.rationale: `attachments/credential-inventory.md` "The operator's keystrokes" section hands over the exact `bao kv put` command for the git token and the exact `ansible-playbook playbooks/site-openbao.yml` command for the policy grant, plus the PAT-mint note. This test-phase session ran no `ansible-playbook`, no `bao kv put`/`write`, and minted no token — confirmed against this session's own tool-call history (git, read, grep and Jenkins-API calls only). The boundary held throughout the slice.

items.description: Nothing in slice 009's half is built here: no `argocd-hooks` namespace, no `tf-presync` ServiceAccount or RBAC, no ExternalSecret, no ApplicationSet parameter. And nothing touches `support/iac-image/`, srviac's `iac-agent` AppRole or its `/etc/iac/secrets.yaml`.
items.rationale: Grepped `/work/Ansible`, `/work/ArgoCDTools` and `/work/Charts` for `argocd-hooks` namespace/RBAC objects, `kind: Namespace`/`ServiceAccount`/`RoleBinding`/`ClusterRole` manifests, and `ExternalSecret`/`ApplicationSet` resources: no matches beyond descriptive prose (a comment in openbao.yml) and pre-existing, unrelated `homelab-shared` library-chart helpers (`_helpers.tpl`, untouched by this slice's commits). `git diff eacb2d0..cd4fded --stat -- support/iac-image/` is empty. `support/iac-agent/etc/iac/secrets.example.yaml` carries no commits from this slice (`git log` shows only pre-existing history).

items.area: The cross-slice export — the four-argument contract in the documents
items.description: The `argo-cd` document set states the four-argument contract everywhere it stated three, so a planner reading only that set builds slice 009's ApplicationSet with four parameters: design.md's flow step, its Job skeleton, the sentence naming the arguments and the ApplicationSet `parameters:` block, with the namespace carrying the same `<app>-<stage>` expression the set already computes for `destination.namespace`; and D29/D33 say the reattach's namespace is passed rather than derived. Written as if it had always been true — no supersession notices in the register.
items.rationale: Independently re-read: `argo-cd/design.md` flow step 1 (327-330), the Job skeleton's `args:` block (378-382), the `required`-guard sentence (391-392) and the ApplicationSet `parameters:` block (196-204) all name four arguments, with `hook.namespace`'s value byte-identical to `destination.namespace`'s expression (207) and an explicit cross-reference note (225-226). `decisions.md` D29 (218-224) and D33 (271-288) both state the reattach's namespace is handed to the hook as an argument, not derived by it.

items.area: The cross-slice export — the credential model in the documents
items.description: The `argo-cd` set states the enumerated-leaves credential model wherever it named the dedicated AppRole: phases.md A.2's own credential line, D33's list of what ESO provisions, and D41's account of what bounds a hook run. D41's blast radius is stated as what it now is — exactly the enumerated provider credentials, not a KV prefix spanning every app — and says that it is tighter than what it replaced. The set also says that the same Secret carries the run's non-secret per-cluster configuration, so a planner authoring the ExternalSecret from it and from this slice's inventory produces the whole of what a run receives.
items.rationale: Independently re-read: `argo-cd/phases.md:39-43` states the enumerated-leaves model and explicitly "No AppRole is minted for the hook"; `decisions.md` D33 (271-288) and D41 (360-377) both describe enumerated leaves, and D41 states explicitly what the model is tighter than (a run-time AppRole/credential-provider identity bound by a KV prefix spanning every app); `design.md:339-342` (flow step 4) names the one Secret as the source of both credentials and non-secret per-cluster configuration. `attachments/credential-inventory.md:70-76`'s "Release identity" bullet says the entrypoint *exports* `TF_VAR_stage`/`TF_VAR_namespace` and that `TF_VAR_cluster` is deliberately not exported. A repo-wide grep of `argo-cd/*.md` for "AppRole" found no live (non-historical) sentence claiming the hook gets its own AppRole — only `history.md` narrates the change, per the set's own written-as-if-always-true convention.

items.area: The root cause — the doc plan names the set
items.description: `slice-doc-plan.md` carries the `argo-cd` document set as a surface, distinguished from the homelab `decisions.md` it is easily confused with, so slices 008–012 inherit the fix instead of each rediscovering the ambiguity.
items.rationale: `docs/slice-doc-plan.md` (read in full, 80 lines) now has six numbered surfaces; surface 2 (21-34) is the `argo-cd/` document set, placed directly after surface 1, with an explicit "Its `decisions.md` is not surface 1" sentence distinguishing the two, and no hardcoded slice numbers (008-012) anywhere in the entry.
